steps.u: The Android app crashes on the settings screen when the user rotates the phone. Stack trace says NullPointerException in SettingsFragment.

steps.a: The ViewModel keeps a callback to the old fragment instance. After rotation the fragment is recreated, but the callback still calls refresh on the destroyed one, whose adapter is null. It is a lifecycle leak, not a simple null check problem.

i.new_string: override fun onViewCreated(v: View, s: Bundle?){ viewModel.items.observe(viewLifecycleOwner){ adapter?.submit(it) } }

steps.a: The settings screen now observes LiveData with the view lifecycle, so rotation recreates the observer and no stale fragment is referenced.

reference.summary: Fixed an Android crash on rotating the settings screen: the view model held a callback to a destroyed fragment; replaced it with lifecycle-aware LiveData observation.
facts: view model kept a callback to the destroyed fragment
replaced by LiveData observed with the view lifecycle

decisions.choice: observe LiveData with the view lifecycle instead of adding a null check
decisions.reason: the callback referenced a destroyed fragment so a null check would hide the leak
